title: Infosys, TCS and Cognizant Slash H-1B Lottery Entries as US Rules Tighten, CRS Finds
headline: Infosys, TCS and Cognizant Slash H-1B Lottery Entries as US Rules Tighten, CRS Finds
subheadline: Cognizant filed no FY2027 registrations at all, Infosys cut entries 91% and TCS 95%, according to a Congressional Research Service report — as a wage-weighted lottery, higher proposed wages and new fees reshape what Trump's work visa changes mean for foreign workers.

body:
• Infosys submitted 759 H-1B registrations for FY2027, down from 8,886; TCS fell to 284 from 5,955; Cognizant recorded none, down from 3,752, according to a Congressional Research Service report dated October 14.
  • Eligible registrations across the FY2027 lottery fell 38.5% overall, and initial petitions from cap-exempt employers for consular processing dropped 91% in the first eight months the $100,000 fee was in effect.
  • The administration replaced the random lottery with a wage-weighted selection in February 2026 and has proposed raising entry-level prevailing wages from about the 17th to the 34th percentile — a change the Labor Department estimates would add $1.46 billion in first-year employer costs.
  • What this means for you: selection now rewards higher-wage offers — under the weighted system the highest wage level gets four lottery entries and the lowest gets one — so entry-level and lower-paid roles face sharply worse odds.

Three of the largest sponsors of Indian technology workers in the United States have all but withdrawn from the H-1B lottery. Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services and Cognizant submitted 91%, 95% and 100% fewer registrations respectively for the fiscal 2027 lottery than for fiscal 2026, according to a Congressional Research Service report titled "H-1B Executive Actions in 2026," reported by The American Bazaar. The figures track registrations, not workers ultimately hired, and the report does not establish that any single policy caused each company's decision.

The Scale of the Pullback

Infosys submitted 759 registrations for fiscal 2027, compared with 8,886 in fiscal 2026. TCS registered 284 candidates, down from 5,955. Cognizant recorded no registrations in the fiscal 2027 figures, compared with 3,752 the previous year. The company-level cuts came alongside a broader contraction: eligible registrations across the FY2027 lottery fell 38.5% from the previous year, according to USCIS data cited in coverage of the CRS report.

https://x.com/moulync/status/2115117603463336080

The retreat extends beyond the lottery. DHS data show that during the first eight months the $100,000 fee was in effect, initial H-1B petitions for consular processing from cap-exempt employers dropped 91% from the same period the year before.

What Changed in the Rules

The CRS assessment, summarized by IANS, examines executive actions affecting wages, selection, employment conditions and the ability of foreign professionals to remain in the United States. In February 2026 the administration replaced the random lottery with a weighted selection process favouring higher-paid, more highly skilled applicants, first applied to employment beginning in October. Under the weighted design, registrations at the highest wage level receive four entries, the next levels three and two, and entry-level wages just one.

In March, the Department of Labor proposed increasing required wages: entry-level prevailing wage requirements would rise from approximately the 17th percentile of comparable local wages to the 34th percentile, with substantial increases for more experienced workers. The Labor Department estimated the wage changes would increase employers' costs by approximately $1.46 billion in the first year. The report also identifies a proposed $103,265 fee for certain petitions, separate from the $100,000 fee imposed in September 2025 on employers bringing new H-1B workers from overseas — a fee the congressional assessment notes has been temporarily blocked by litigation. Already in force are an extension of the $4,000 biometric fee to certain H-1B and L-1 extension petitions and expanded scrutiny of employers suspected of misusing the programme. In September 2026, DHS also proposed eliminating the 60-day grace period after employment ends, and in October it eliminated automatic extensions of work authorization for spouses of H-1B workers.

What It Means for Foreign Workers

For Indian professionals, the combined effect is a narrower door at every stage: fewer sponsors filing, a lottery that rewards the highest-paid offers, higher wage floors employers must meet, and less security after a job ends. Workers in senior, high-salary roles in fields such as AI, data engineering and cybersecurity are best positioned under the weighted system. Recent graduates and entry-level hires — historically a large share of the big IT firms' US intake — face the steepest decline in chances, which is precisely the segment the registration collapse measures.
